properties.procedure: The seeds were tied in a muslin cloth (pottali) and subjected to boiling in cow’s milk at 60 °C for 3 hours, followed by washing and air-drying.
Dehulled and powdered Croton tiglium seeds were tied in a cloth bundle and boiled in milk for 3 h, then washed and dried; the process was repeated three times for purification.
Seeds were cleaned, tied in a cloth pouch, and subjected to boiling in milk for 3 hours, then washed with hot water, ground, smeared on earthen plates, sun-dried, and stored as purified Jayapala.
The processed seeds were triturated with fresh lemon juice in a mortar–pestle for 1 hour daily for 3 days and air-dried after each cycle to obtain a uniform paste.
